title: Integration discovery with Nova Finance - Redwood inference
summary: Discovery focused on integration options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy architecture, rate limiting and quotas, and observability hooks. Customer wants a pilot on dedicated capacity to validate latency and cost for their fraud-detection pipeline; security team requested SOC2/HSM/KMS info and network topology for VPC deployment.
topics: Integration patterns: SDK vs HTTP gateway
Rate limits, quotas, and concurrency controls
Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
action_items: Lena Park - Send dedicated pricing sheet + pilot contract template by 2026-11-27
Marco Ruiz - Share LangChain/LlamaIndex example repo and a short demo notebook by 2026-11-26
Jia Chen - Run perf baseline with sample payloads and share latency numbers (p50/p95) by 2026-12-03
Samir Patel (customer) - Share security questionnaire and network diagram by 2026-11-30
next_steps: Send security pack (SOC2, ISO docs, KMS/HSM architecture)
Provide LangChain/LlamaIndex starter repo and SDK snippets
Schedule a Dedicated capacity pilot kickoff (SE-led bench) next week
notes: Shared artifacts mentioned: Redwood Dedicated deck (link), LangChain examples repo (github.com/redwood/lang-examples), pilot benchmark spreadsheet (drive.redwood/pilot-novafin). Links are notes in CRM; not attached here.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Marco, our SE. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Aisha Khan: Hi all, Aisha here.
[00:11] Ben Lowe: Ben, hey.
[00:13] Samir Patel: Samir, security.
[00:15] Maya Ortiz: Maya, platform.
[00:17] Lena Park: Great, thanks. Agenda for today — integration patterns, SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy options for routing, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. We'll leave time for Qs and next steps.
[00:34] Marco Ruiz: Quick context question: Ben, could you say how you're planning to call the models today — is this inline in your fraud pipeline, or async batch?
[00:42] Ben Lowe: Mostly inline — sub 200ms p50 target for fraud scoring, p95 can be up to 600ms... we also have nightly re-runs that can be batched.
[00:53] Marco Ruiz: Got it. That is helpful. For sub-200ms we typically recommend either our Hosted with optimised small models or Dedicated with pinned GPUs and KV caching.
[01:05] Ben Lowe: Can you remind me how KV cache works? Is that local to the GPU?
[01:10] Marco Ruiz: Yes, the KV cache is kept on the serving nodes to avoid re-computing prefixes; helps for repeated context. Sorry sometimes the transcription says K-V cash, but it's KV cache, cache.
[01:21] Aisha Khan: We're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — security will likely push for VPC or Private if we can't live with hosted data residency. Samir?
[01:29] Samir Patel: Right, basic checks: SOC2 type II, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and importantly KMS integration and support for HSM-backed keys if possible.
[01:39] Lena Park: We do support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated with VPC peering; we can share the security pack.
[01:45] Samir Patel: Also need network topology for on-prem routing and any egress pins.
[01:49] Marco Ruiz: We'll include a VPC diagram. For gateway/proxy, do you plan to put a sidecar proxy in front of Redwood or route traffic through your existing API gateway?
[01:58] Maya Ortiz: We'd prefer to re-use our gateway and have a proxy that can mutate headers for tenant id and enforce rate limiting.
[02:06] Marco Ruiz: That's supported. Many customers run a lightweight gateway that inserts X-Redwood-Tenant header and does token-level metering.
[02:13] Evan Brooks: What about LangChain and LlamaIndex — we use LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex for vectorized retrieval. Any native connectors?
[02:22] Marco Ruiz: Yes — we have SDK examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. The LangChain connector is basically a small adapter using our Python SDK; the LlamaIndex lineage is a connector to the embeddings endpoint. I'll share the repo, though sometimes the docs show "Lang Chain" instead of LangChain.
[02:36] Ben Lowe: Are there any prebuilt retriever components or do we need to implement ourselves?
[02:40] Marco Ruiz: There are starter retrievers; most teams wire LlamaIndex to our embeddings API, store vectors in your vector DB, and then orchestrate retrieval. We also provide sample notebooks that show a full pipeline.
[02:51] Aisha Khan: How do you handle rate limits/quotas? We have multiple services hitting the layer and want per-tenant quotas.
[02:58] Lena Park: We have per-api-key quotas at the platform level, plus per-route throttles you can configure. For Dedicated we can do tenant isolation and apply quotas per workspace.
[03:09] Samir Patel: Does the rate limiter live in your gateway or ours?
[03:13] Marco Ruiz: Typically your gateway enforces burst controls and our endpoint will enforce global quotas — it's a shared responsibility. For Private deployment you can run the rate-limiter internally.
[03:24] Ben Lowe: Any hard limits on concurrency or token rate per second we should be aware of?
[03:29] Marco Ruiz: On Hosted there are default concurrency limits per account (we'll share exact numbers); on Dedicated you can set concurrency based on reserved GPU slots. We can also configure autoscale policies for burst.
[03:41] Evan Brooks: Observability: we need token-level cost attribution and per-route latency breakdown.
[03:46] Lena Park: Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdown per request id; we also expose traces and an export stream to your tracing system (Zipkin/Jaeger or Datadog).
[03:58] Maya Ortiz: Do you have SDK hooks to propagate our trace ids?
[04:01] Marco Ruiz: Yes, the SDK supports passing X-Request-Id and trace headers; we auto-link traces in the Console.
[04:09] Ben Lowe: And logs/audit? We need immutable audit logs for regulatory review.
[04:14] Lena Park: Audit logs can be exported to your S3 or to our retention for enterprise tiers. We'll include retention SLAs in the security pack.
[04:25] Samir Patel: For KMS — can you describe key flow for Private?
[04:29] Marco Ruiz: For Private, keys can be customer-managed; requests encrypt model data at rest with your keys. On Dedicated in a VPC we can integrate with your cloud KMS; HSM options available for the enterprise package. We'll send a diagram.
[04:44] Ben Lowe: Regarding SDKs, what languages do you support?
[04:47] Marco Ruiz: Official SDKs for Python, Node, and Go; the Python SDK has the tightest LangChain integrations. We also have a low-level REST API for gateways.
[04:56] Aisha Khan: If we run a Dedicated pilot, how quickly can you provision capacity?
[05:01] Lena Park: We can provision a small Dedicated pool in 2–3 weeks, pilot-friendly. Production-sized pools have longer lead times.
[05:07] Ben Lowe: For the pilot, can we test with our real payloads so we get realistic latency?
[05:11] Marco Ruiz: Absolutely. If you can share sample requests and 24hr traffic profile, our SEs will run a baseline and p50/p95 numbers.
[05:20] Ben Lowe: We'll share a sample set — note some requests have long prompt histories (2–3k tokens), others are small.
[05:27] Marco Ruiz: That matters for kernel selection and KV cache sizing.
[05:31] Aisha Khan: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex retrieving embeddings? We use a managed vector DB.
[05:36] Marco Ruiz: Works fine — LlamaIndex calls our embedding endpoint; we return consistent vector shapes. Watch for rate limits on embeddings; we can batch.
[05:45] Evan Brooks: What about routing to fallback models if capacity constrained?
[05:50] Marco Ruiz: We support automatic fallback policies — route to a cheaper quantized variant or to a hosted tier. You can set policies by latency or cost thresholds.
[06:00] Maya Ortiz: How does cost attribution work if we fallback?
[06:03] Lena Park: Console attributes cost per-request including fallback hops; you get a per-request cost breakdown.
[06:10] Ben Lowe: For the network flow, do you accept requests coming from a proxy inside our VPC?
[06:15] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we have options: VPC peering, private link, or a gateway proxy. In Private deployments you can run a local control plane and keep data on-prem.
[06:26] Samir Patel: Data retention — can we set retention to zero for certain endpoints?
[06:30] Lena Park: Yes, we have data retention policies by route and model. We can set no retention for PII-sensitive endpoints.
[06:36] Evan Brooks: Any sample code for LangChain with your streaming responses? We rely on streaming for UI latency.
[06:42] Marco Ruiz: The Python SDK supports SSE/streaming; LangChain adapter has a streaming callback class in the examples repo. I'll share the snippet.
[06:53] Ben Lowe: One more, do you have an NPM/Node example for server-side rendering where we synthesize embeddings and generate?
[06:59] Marco Ruiz: Yes, Node SDK has both embeddings and generation examples.
[07:04] Lena Park: I want to make sure we document the next steps. Marco, you'll share the LangChain/LlamaIndex repo and the perf notebook. Jia will run the baseline. I'll send pilot pricing and security pack. Samir will send questionnaire.
[07:19] Samir Patel: I'll send the network diagram and security questionnaire.
[07:22] Aisha Khan: Timeline — we'd like to kick pilot in the first week of December. Is that feasible?
[07:27] Lena Park: Yes, that's feasible. We'll aim to have pilot contract and provisioning plan by Nov 30.
[07:33] Evan Brooks: Questions from the engineering side: does Redwood support per-tenant model pinning? We want to pin a specific quantized variant for latency.
[07:42] Marco Ruiz: Yes, per-workspace model pins are supported; rollout controls let you canary between variants.
[07:49] Ben Lowe: Any administrative SDK for programmatic quota changes?
[07:53] Marco Ruiz: Admin API exists for quota management; we can enable a scoped API token for your platform team.
[08:00] Maya Ortiz: For observability hook exports — how frequent and do you support streaming exports?
[08:06] Lena Park: We support streaming exports via webhook or pushing to your Kafka/S3 bucket; telemetry batch cadence can be configured.
[08:15] Ben Lowe: Great.
[08:17] Marco Ruiz: I'll note a few follow-up items: in the repo there is an example of a gateway config that mutates tenant headers and enforces per-tenant rate limits — that's worked well for other fintechs.
[08:28] Aisha Khan: Ok, wrapping up from our side — main blockers are security sign-off and a quick production-like benchmark.
[08:35] Lena Park: Understood. We'll prioritize the security pack and run baseline after you provide sample payloads.
[08:41] Evan Brooks: Can you also share rough cost estimates for 500k tokens/day on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[08:46] Lena Park: We'll include a cost comparison in the pricing sheet.
[08:50] Samir Patel: Also, please include HSM options and expected procurement steps.
[08:54] Lena Park: Will do.
[08:57] Marco Ruiz: Any final technical Qs?
[09:00] Ben Lowe: None from me.
[09:02] Maya Ortiz: All good.
[09:04] Lena Park: Thanks everyone. Recap: we'll send security docs, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, perf notebook, and pricing. Proposed pilot kickoff first week of December. I'll follow-up with a calendar invite.
[09:18] (meeting end)
end_summary: Customer (Nova Finance) is evaluating Redwood for a fraud scoring pipeline that needs low-latency inline calls and batched re-runs. Key integration points: SDKs (Python/Node/Go), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors and examples, gateway/proxy header mutation and per-tenant quotas, observability hooks for traces and token-level cost, and security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS/HSM). Next steps: share security pack, LangChain/LlamaIndex repo, perf baseline, and pricing; target pilot first week of December.
